question: Does 'West Route' on Dragontail duplicate 'Pandora's Box'?
answer: Yes, the same climb, and it is already handled: same-climb-read.json records wa_dragontail_peak_west_route merged into wa_dragontail_peak_r3 (migration 0400), and allRoutesOnPeak now holds only r3 'Pandora's Box (W Couloir)'. Research agrees with that merge. The West Route is the standard Colchuck Col route: up the Colchuck Glacier to Colchuck Col, then the couloir just east of the col to a notch in the ridge (the notch is Pandora's Box, and the couloir below it often takes the name too), a downclimb or bypass, and a snow-and-rock traverse to the summit. Mountaineers pages and a 2020 write-up put the two names together ('West Route, Pandora's Box'). A ski report treats the box as a false summit and the couloir as a separate feature, but that is a naming quirk, not a second line. Not to be confused with Colchuck Col Buttress (5.6 rock buttress, its own row) or the Aasgard Pass East Route.
recommendation: No change to the merge. Optionally show 'West Route' as the alias of r3 (guidebook name; Pandora's Box is the popular one). Two data flags on the surviving row r3: (1) it is stored discipline 'alpine' with grade 'Class 3', but the climb is a non-technical snow couloir with a Class 4 bypass and no 5.x, which is 'mountaineering' under the owner's rule; (2) its stored name carries '(W Couloir)'; consider 'West Route (Pandora's Box)'.
evidence: https://gethighonaltitude.com/2020/06/25/dragontail-peak-west-route/ - page title 'West Route', technical line 'West Route, Pandora's Box', Colchuck Col, couloir, short downclimb to the upper plateau (June)
